mainTopic: The execution of the זקן ממרא, public announcements of executions, and the punishments and examples of false prophets
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about a זקן ממרא who rules that one should add to ציצית or תפילין. Using רבי זירא's rule about an outer compartment that does not see the air, the גמרא shows that an extra compartment always ruins the תפילין. A new משנה then teaches where and when the זקן ממרא is executed. רבי עקיבא says he is executed at the בית דין הגדול in ירושלים during the רגל. רבי יהודה says the פסוק requires only that people 'hear,' so he is executed right away and letters announce it. A ברייתא lists four sinners whose execution must be announced, and explains why the פסוק about עדים זוממין says 'those who remain.' The next משנה teaches that a false prophet and one who prophesies in the name of an idol are executed by the court, while three other prophecy sins are punished בידי שמים. It also lists more cases of חנק, including the exception for the plotting witnesses against a בת כהן. The גמרא brings the פסוקים behind each group and gives examples: צדקיה בן כנענה, who should have noticed that all the prophets used identical wording; חנניה בן עזור, who announced his own קל וחומר as prophecy; the prophets of the בעל; and יונה. The example for one who ignores a prophet's words continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Adding to ציצית ruins the מצוה from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier answer: if the upper knot of ציצית is required by Torah law, then tying in an extra string ruins the מצוה from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the upper knot is required by Torah law, the מצוה is already ruined from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it began before this section. It explains that adding a string to ציצית is not really 'adding,' because tying it in ruins the מצוה from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The upper knot binds all the strings together. If that knot is a Torah requirement, an extra string tied in becomes part of the ציצית and spoils them. So this case is not one of adding to a valid מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: the upper knot of the ציצית strings

phrases.english: that the upper knot is from the Torah,
it is already ruined from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer from the previous daf about ציצית.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the case is not 'adding' at all, because the addition ruins the מצוה from the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: Adding a string to ציצית is a case of ruining the מצוה, not adding to it.

steps.title: Shouldn't תפילין work the same way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: with תפילין too, an extra compartment placed alongside stands separately, and תפילין made with five compartments are ruined from the start, so where is the case of adding?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, תפילין should be the same! If he made four compartments and then brought another and placed it next to them, these stand by themselves and that one stands by itself. And if he made five compartments, they are ruined from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer about ציצית by applying the same reasoning to תפילין. It argues that with תפילין there is also no real case of adding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to add a fifth compartment. If it is set down next to the four, it is separate and does not count as part of them. If the תפילין are made with five from the start, they are invalid from the beginning. Either way, it seems there is no true 'adding' case for the זקן ממרא to be liable for.

phrases.english: If so, תפילין too?
If he made four compartments,
and brought another and placed it next to them –
these stand by themselves
and that one stands by itself.
And if he made five compartments –
it is ruined from the start!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reasoning of step 1 to תפילין.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a זקן ממרא can be liable for ruling to add a fifth compartment to תפילין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ציצית reasoning is correct, תפילין also have no real 'adding' case: a separate compartment does not join, and five compartments made together are invalid from the start.

steps.title: רבי זירא: an outer compartment that does not see the air is invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רבי זירא's rule: if an outer compartment is not exposed to the air, the תפילין are invalid. So placing an extra compartment next to them does affect them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי זירא said: an outer compartment that does not see the air is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by quoting a rule from רבי זירא. This shows that an extra compartment always ruins the תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that a fifth compartment placed alongside simply 'stands by itself.' רבי זירא teaches that an outer compartment blocked from the air makes the תפילין invalid. So adding a fifth compartment always affects the four, unlike the challenge's first case.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't he say? (brings a known teaching)
exposed to the air (literally, 'sees the air')

phrases.english: But didn't רבי זירא say:

phrases.aramaic: בַּיִת חִיצוֹן שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָאֲוִיר –
phrases.english: an outer compartment that does not see the air –
phrases.notes: Once a fifth one is placed beside it, the end compartment is closed in on that side.

phrases.english: is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an outside rule showing that the challenge's 'stands by itself' case does not apply to תפילין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A fifth compartment set beside the four stays separate and does no harm.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of רבי זירא's rule, adding a fifth compartment always ruins the תפילין.
steps.whatToRemember: With תפילין, an extra compartment always affects the others, because an outer compartment cut off from the air is invalid.

steps.title: משנה: רבי עקיבא — the זקן ממרא is executed in ירושלים during the רגל
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that the זקן ממרא is not executed in his own town or in יבנה. He is brought to the בית דין הגדול in ירושלים, kept until the רגל, and executed then, so that all the people will hear and fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We do not execute him in the court of his city or in the court of יבנה. Instead, he is brought up to the בית דין הגדול in ירושלים, guarded until the רגל, and executed during the רגל, as it says: 'And all the people shall hear and fear and no longer act wickedly.' These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and tells us where and when the זקן ממרא is put to death. This is רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even יבנה, where the סנהדרין sat later, is not enough. The execution must happen at the בית דין הגדול in ירושלים during the רגל, when crowds are there. The פסוק 'all the people shall hear and fear' is the source for making it public.

keyTerms.meaning: the town where the סנהדרין later sat

phrases.english: משנה:
We do not execute him
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the זקן ממרא, the elder who rules against the בית דין הגדול.

phrases.english: not in the court of his city,
and not in the court of יבנה,
rather, they bring him up
to the Great Court in ירושלים.
And they guard him until the festival,
and they execute him during the festival,
as it says: 'And all the people shall hear and fear
phrases.notes: דברים 17:13

phrases.english: and no longer act wickedly.'
These are the words of רבי עקיבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מְמִיתִין אוֹתוֹ לֹא בְּבֵית דִּין שֶׁבְּעִירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about carrying out the זקן ממרא's punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, the זקן ממרא is executed by the בית דין הגדול in ירושלים during the רגל, to make it public.

steps.title: משנה: רבי יהודה — execute him right away and send out notices
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה argues that we do not delay his punishment. He is executed immediately, and letters are sent everywhere announcing that this man was sentenced to death by the court.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: We do not delay this man's judgment. Instead, we execute him right away, and write and send messengers to all places: 'So-and-so was sentenced to death by the court.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with רבי עקיבא about the timing. He says to carry out the punishment at once and make it public through written notices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that people need to hear about it. They disagree on how. רבי עקיבא waits for the crowds at the רגל, while רבי יהודה does not allow the delay and spreads the news by letter.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְעַנִּין אֶת דִּינוֹ שֶׁל זֶה,
phrases.english: We do not delay the judgment of this one,
rather, we execute him immediately,
and we write and send messengers
to all the places:
'So-and-so was sentenced to death by the court.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין מְעַנִּין אֶת דִּינוֹ שֶׁל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי עקיבא's view in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the זקן ממרא is executed immediately, and the public is told through letters sent everywhere.
steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת: רבי עקיבא waits for the רגל so the crowds will see it; רבי יהודה does not delay and announces it by letter.

steps.title: The ברייתא restates רבי עקיבא's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא that repeats רבי עקיבא's position from the משנה. This sets up the ברייתא's continuation, which comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: We do not execute him in the court of his city or in the court of יבנה. Instead, he is brought up to the בית דין הגדול in ירושלים, guarded until the רגל, and executed during the רגל, as it says: 'And all the people shall hear and fear.' These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that repeats רבי עקיבא's view. This is a setup step: the ברייתא goes on to show how רבי יהודה responds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is almost the same as the משנה, with only the first part of the פסוק quoted. The ברייתא is brought because it continues past what the משנה says, so its first part is laid out here as groundwork.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the משנה being repeated by mistake. It is a ברייתא, a separate teaching, which the גמרא quotes because it continues further than the משנה.

phrases.english: גמרא: The רבנן taught:
We do not execute him
not in the court of his city
and not in the court of יבנה,
rather, they bring him up
to the Great Court in ירושלים
and they guard him until the festival,
and they execute him during the festival,
as it says: 'And all the people shall hear and fear.'
phrases.notes: דברים 17:13

phrases.english: These are the words of רבי עקיבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מְמִיתִין אוֹתוֹ לֹא בְּבֵית דִּין שֶׁבְּעִירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה by quoting a ברייתא that restates רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא repeats that, according to רבי עקיבא, the זקן ממרא is executed in ירושלים during the רגל.

steps.title: רבי יהודה challenges רבי עקיבא from the wording of the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה points out that the פסוק says 'hear and fear,' not 'see and fear,' so the people do not need to watch the execution.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said to him: Does the פסוק say 'they will see and fear'? It only says 'they will hear and fear'!
steps.whatsHappening: Still inside the ברייתא, רבי יהודה pushes back against רבי עקיבא's reason for waiting until the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא held that the execution waits for the festival so the crowds will be there. רבי יהודה says the פסוק only requires that people hear about it, not see it. So gathering a crowd is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: They will hear and fear (the actual wording of the פסוק)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי עקיבא, whose view the ברייתא just quoted.

phrases.english: Is it stated, "They shall see and fear"?
But isn't it stated only, "They shall hear and fear"!
phrases.notes: דברים 17:13

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי עקיבא's position quoted in the ברייתא in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's rule that the זקן ממרא is held until the רגל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says 'hear,' not 'see,' so the crowd does not need to be present at the execution.

steps.title: Execute him right away and send out written notices
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that the execution should not be delayed. Instead, the court sends letters everywhere announcing the sentence.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why delay this man's judgment? Rather, we execute him right away, and write and send to every place: 'So-and-so was sentenced to death by the court.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives his own ruling, which follows from his reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the goal is only that people hear, holding the man until the festival is an unnecessary delay of justice. Written notices sent everywhere fulfill 'they will hear and fear.' This is the same view as in step 5, now with its reason from the פסוק.

phrases.english: Why delay the judgment of this one?
Rather, they execute him immediately,
and they write and send to every place:
"So-and-so was sentenced to death in court."

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: wait for the רגל so the crowds see. רבי יהודה: the פסוק says 'hear,' so execute right away and send notices.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical ruling from the challenge in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The זקן ממרא is executed immediately, and the verdict is publicized by letters.

steps.title: Four sinners whose execution must be publicly announced
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four sinners whose death sentences require a public announcement.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Four need a public announcement: the מסית, the בן סורר ומורה, the זקן ממרא, and עדים זוממין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists all the cases where the court must announce the execution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זקן ממרא is not the only case with an announcement. Three other sinners also need one, and the next line explains where this comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: One who entices others to worship idols
Plotting witnesses who are proven to have lied

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Four require a public announcement:
the one who entices, and the stubborn and rebellious son,
and the rebellious elder, and plotting witnesses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the topic of announcing executions beyond the זקן ממרא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מסית, בן סורר ומורה, זקן ממרא, and עדים זוממין all require a public announcement.

steps.title: Why the verse for plotting witnesses says 'those who remain'
steps.stepSummary: The other three cases use 'all the nation' or 'all Israel,' but the פסוק for עדים זוממין says 'those who remain.' Why the difference?
steps.simpleTranslation: In all of them it is written 'and all the nation' or 'all Israel.' Why with עדים זוממין is it written 'and those who remain'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows the source for the announcement in each case and notices that one פסוק uses different wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the four פסוקים says the people will 'hear and fear,' which is the source for the announcement. Three say 'all the nation' or 'all Israel,' but the עדים זוממין פסוק says 'those who remain.' The ברייתא asks what that change teaches.

phrases.english: In all of them it is written about them
"And all the nation" or "all Israel."
phrases.notes: דברים 17:13; דברים 13:12; דברים 21:21

phrases.english: With plotting witnesses, it is written "and those who remain"?
phrases.notes: דברים 19:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks at the פסוקים behind the list in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the עדים זוממין פסוק says 'those who remain' instead of 'all the nation.'

steps.title: Not everyone is fit to be a witness
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'those who remain' because the warning is aimed only at people who are fit to testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because not everyone is fit to give testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question in one short line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lesson of עדים זוממין is about lying in testimony. Only people who can serve as witnesses need that warning. So the פסוק speaks to 'those who remain,' meaning those fit to testify, and not to the entire nation.

phrases.english: Because not everyone is fit for testimony.

steps.whatToRemember: Four sinners need a public announcement. For עדים זוממין, the פסוק is aimed only at people who are fit to testify.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The warning is limited to those fit to testify, since not everyone can be a witness.

steps.title: The false prophet is executed by a human court
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a נביא השקר who prophesies what he did not hear, or what was told to someone else, is put to death by the court.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A false prophet, who prophesies what he did not hear, or what was not said to him, is put to death by human hands.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins on a new topic: the death penalty of the נביא השקר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two types count as a נביא השקר: one who made up a prophecy completely, and one who repeats a real prophecy that was given to a different prophet. Both are executed by בית דין, not left to Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: His death is by human hands (a court execution)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The false prophet
who prophesies what he did not hear,
and what was not said to him,
phrases.notes: This is a real prophecy, but it was given to a different prophet, not to him.

phrases.english: his death is at the hand of man.

steps.confusionAlert: 'What was not said to him' does not mean a made-up prophecy. That is the first case. It means a real message that God gave to someone else.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the זקן ממרא discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A prophet who invents a prophecy, or claims one given to another prophet, is executed by בית דין.

steps.title: Three prophecy sins punished by Heaven
steps.stepSummary: One who holds back his prophecy, one who ignores a prophet's words, and a prophet who disobeys his own prophecy all die בידי שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one who holds back his prophecy, one who ignores the words of a prophet, and a prophet who goes against his own words: their death is by the hands of Heaven, as it says 'I will demand it of him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with three contrasting cases that are not punished by the court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אבל' (but) sets these apart from the נביא השקר. These three are not executed by בית דין. God Himself punishes them, as the פסוק says 'I will demand it of him.'

keyTerms.meaning: One who holds back (suppresses) his prophecy
One who disregards a prophet's words
His death is by the hands of Heaven
I will demand it of him

phrases.english: But one who suppresses his prophecy,
and one who disregards the words of a prophet,
and a prophet who violated his own words,
his death is at the hand of Heaven,
as it is stated: "I will demand it of him."
phrases.notes: דברים 18:19

steps.whatToRemember: נביא השקר (invents a prophecy, or takes another prophet's) = court execution. Holding back a prophecy, ignoring a prophet, or a prophet disobeying his own prophecy = death בידי שמים.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 12: these cases are punished by Heaven, not by the court.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suppressing a prophecy, ignoring a prophet, or a prophet violating his own prophecy is punished by death בידי שמים.

steps.title: A prophet who speaks in the name of an idol
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds to its list a person who prophesies in the name of עבודה זרה. He is guilty even if his ruling happens to be correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who prophesies in the name of an idol and says, "This is what the idol said," is killed by חנק. This is true even if the הלכה he announced was correct, calling impure what really is impure and pure what really is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of people killed by חנק. Now it adds a prophet who claims his message comes from an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sin here is not giving a wrong ruling. The sin is speaking in the name of עבודה זרה. That is why he is still killed even when his ruling about טומאה and טהרה is exactly right.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of an idol
He hit on the correct halacha
To declare impure / to declare pure

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think he is punished for a wrong ruling. Even a correct ruling is a capital sin when it is said in the name of an idol.

phrases.english: One who prophesies in the name of idol worship,
phrases.notes: The punishment isn't repeated here. We are still inside the משנה's list of people killed by חנק.

phrases.english: and says: "This is what the idol said,"
even if he hit upon the correct halacha
to declare impure what is impure
and to declare pure what is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of those killed by חנק, moving from נביא השקר to one who prophesies in the name of an idol.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who prophesies in the name of עבודה זרה is killed by חנק, even if his ruling is correct.

steps.title: Sinning with a married woman after נישואין
steps.stepSummary: Once a woman has entered her husband's home for נישואין, a man who sins with her is killed by חנק, even if the marriage has not yet been consummated.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone has relations with a married woman, then once she has entered her husband's home for marriage, even if she has not yet been with her husband, the man who has relations with her is killed by חנק.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds another case to the חנק list: a man who sins with an אשת איש. It also tells us the exact point from which this law applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding moment is her entering the husband's domain for נישואין, not their first time together. The word כֵּיוָן ("once") shows the law changes at that moment. Before it, while she is only an engaged נערה המאורסה, the punishment is different (סקילה).

phrases.english: One who has relations with a married woman,
once she has entered her husband's domain for marriage,
even though she has not yet been with him,
one who has relations with her is killed by strangulation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the prophecy cases to the next case on the משנה's חנק list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once she has entered רשות הבעל for נישואין, one who sins with her gets חנק, even before the marriage is consummated.

steps.title: The exception for plotting witnesses against a כהן's daughter
steps.stepSummary: The עדים זוממין against a בת כהן, and the man accused with her, are killed by חנק. This is an exception to the rule that זוממין receive the same death they tried to cause.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also killed by חנק are the plotting witnesses against a כהן's daughter, and the man she sinned with. All plotting witnesses normally get the same death they tried to bring on their victim, except for the plotting witnesses against a כהן's daughter and her partner.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends its חנק list with the עדים זוממין of a בת כהן. It points out that this case breaks the usual rule of הזמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A married בת כהן who sins is killed by שריפה, but the man with her gets the regular חנק. Normally עדים זוממין receive whatever death they plotted. Here, though, the witnesses get חנק and not her שריפה. This is an exception in how הזמה is carried out. They are still fully עדים זוממין.

keyTerms.meaning: That same death (the one they plotted)

steps.whatToRemember: The general rule is that עדים זוממין get the same death they plotted. The one exception the משנה gives is the case of a בת כהן, where the witnesses get חנק instead of her שריפה.
steps.confusionAlert: These witnesses are not being treated as "not זוממין." They are real עדים זוממין. Only their form of death is different.

phrases.english: And the plotting witnesses against a priest's daughter, and her partner,
for all witnesses proven to be plotters
are sent to that same death,
phrases.notes: "That same death" means the death they tried to bring on the person they lied about.

phrases.english: except for the plotters against a priest's daughter and her partner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה's list with a case that is an exception to the general rule of הזמה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זוממי בת כהן receive חנק, not her שריפה. This is the one exception to the rule that זוממין get the death they plotted.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule of כאשר זמם has a known exception in how it is carried out.

steps.title: Three die by the court, three die by Heaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that sorts the sins of prophecy. Three are punished by בית דין, and three are punished בידי שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: three are killed by people, and three die at the hands of Heaven. One who prophesies what he did not hear, one who prophesies what was told to someone else, and one who prophesies in the name of an idol are killed by people. One who holds back his prophecy, one who ignores a prophet's words, and a prophet who disobeys his own words die at the hands of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא. It neatly organizes all the prophecy-related sinners from the משנה into two groups of three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first group sins by saying a false or forbidden prophecy out loud, and בית דין kills them. The second group sins by failing to act on a true prophecy, and their punishment is left to Heaven. The ברייתא gathers together what the משנה listed in separate places.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
One who holds back his prophecy

steps.whatToRemember: There are 3 + 3. Saying a false prophecy (or one in an idol's name) brings death by בית דין. Holding back, ignoring, or disobeying a true prophecy brings death בידי שמים.

phrases.english: GEMARA
The Rabbis taught:
Three: their death is at the hands of man,
and three: their death is at the hands of Heaven.
One who prophesies what he did not hear,
and what was not said to him,
and one who prophesies in the name of idol worship:
their death is at the hands of man.
One who holds back his prophecy,
one who ignores the words of a prophet,
and a prophet who disobeys his own words:
their death is at the hands of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה מִיתָתָן בִּידֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה by bringing a ברייתא that groups the prophecy cases from steps 12–14 into two sets of three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A false prophet, one who repeats another's prophecy, and one who prophesies in an idol's name are killed by בית דין. One who holds back his prophecy, one who ignores a prophet, and a prophet who disobeys himself die בידי שמים.

steps.title: Asking for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the ברייתא's rules about prophets come from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the פסוק behind the ברייתא's list of prophecy sins. This sets up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in step 17 split six sins into two groups: three punished by בית דין and three punished בידי שמים. Now the גמרא wants a Torah source for both groups.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? It asks for a source in the פסוקים.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא quoted in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the punishments listed in the ברייתא.

steps.title: One verse teaches the three sins punished by בית דין
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב reads one פסוק in three parts. Each part matches one of the three sins punished by בית דין, and the punishment is חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'But the prophet who sins on purpose to speak a word in My name.' This is a prophet who says what he did not hear. 'That I did not command him' means I commanded someone else. This is a prophet who says what was told to a different prophet. 'Or who speaks in the name of other gods' is a prophet who speaks in the name of עבודה זרה. And the פסוק says, 'That prophet shall die.' Any death in the Torah that is not described is חנק.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the source for the first group. He splits one פסוק into three parts, one for each of the three sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the פסוק matches a different sin. 'In My name' means he made it up. 'That I did not command HIM' means it was said to another prophet. 'Other gods' means עבודה זרה. The פסוק says 'shall die' without saying how, and the rule is that such a death is חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: I commanded it to his fellow prophet
A death the Torah mentions without saying how
Strangulation, one of the four deaths of בית דין

steps.whatToRemember: One פסוק covers all three sins punished by בית דין. They die by חנק because the פסוק says 'shall die' without describing the death.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
For the verse says:
"But the prophet who sins on purpose
to speak a word in My name."
phrases.notes: דברים 18:20

phrases.english: This is one who prophesies what he did not hear.
"That I did not command him":
this implies that I did command it to his fellow,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַמִּתְנַבֵּא מַה שֶּׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר לוֹ.
phrases.english: This is one who prophesies what was not said to him.
"Or who speaks in the name of other gods":
This is one who prophesies in the name of idol worship.
And it is written: "That prophet shall die."
And every death stated in the Torah without details
is nothing other than strangulation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 for the בית דין group.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דברים 18:20, read in three parts, together with the rule that a death without details is חנק.

steps.title: One verse read three ways teaches the sins punished בידי שמים
steps.stepSummary: The three sins punished בידי שמים all come from one פסוק. Its key word is read in three different ways, and the end of the פסוק shows that God Himself punishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who holds back his prophecy, one who ignores a prophet's words, and a prophet who disobeys his own words all die בידי שמים. The פסוק says, 'The man who will not listen.' Read it as 'will not tell' and as 'will not listen to My words.' And it says, 'I will demand it from him.' That means בידי שמים.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא gives the source for the second group of three. It reads one word in the פסוק three different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יִשְׁמַע ('listen') covers the one who ignores a prophet. Read as יַשְׁמִיעַ ('make heard'), it covers the prophet who holds back his message. Read as יִשָּׁמַע, it covers the prophet who does not follow his own words. 'I will demand' means God punishes, not בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: One who holds back or hides something
One who ignores or gives up on something
Read it as, meaning read the word in another way
I will demand it from him

steps.whatToRemember: The three בידי שמים sins come from one word read three ways. 'I will demand' shows that God, not בית דין, punishes.

phrases.english: One who holds back his prophecy,
and one who ignores the words of a prophet,
and a prophet who disobeys his own words,
their death is at the hand of Heaven.
As it is written: "And the man who will not listen."
phrases.notes: דברים 18:19. Read plainly, this is the person who ignores a prophet.

phrases.english: Read it also as: "will not make heard,"
phrases.notes: Same letters, different vowels. This is the prophet who keeps his message to himself.

phrases.english: And read it also as: "will not heed My words."
phrases.notes: This reading is the prophet who does not follow the message he himself delivered.

phrases.english: And it is written: "I will demand it from him":
this means at the hand of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the source for the second group of the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דברים 18:19, with יִשְׁמַע read three ways, and 'אנכי אדרש' showing death בידי שמים.

steps.title: צדקיה בן כנענה as an example
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives צדקיה בן כנענה as an example of a prophet who said what he did not hear.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who prophesies what he did not hear is someone like צדקיה בן כנענה. As it is written: 'And צדקיהו בן כנענה made himself iron horns.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the first sin in the list and gives a real example from נ״ך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צדקיה made iron horns and told אחאב that he would win his war. God never gave him that message, so he fits the case of one who prophesies what he did not hear.

keyTerms.meaning: A false prophet in the time of אַחְאָב
Iron horns, a symbol of winning the battle

phrases.english: One who prophesies what he did not hear,
for example, Tzidkiya son of Kenaana,
as it is written: "And Tzidkiyahu
son of Kenaana made himself iron horns."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 18:10

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמִּתְנַבֵּא מַה שֶּׁלֹּא שָׁמַע, כְּגוֹן צִדְקִיָּה בֶן כְּנַעֲנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sources to an example of the first sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדקיה בן כנענה is an example of one who prophesies what he did not hear.

steps.title: Why was צדקיה blamed if a spirit fooled him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what צדקיה could have done differently. The פסוקים show that a spirit sent by God tricked him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What should he have done? The spirit of נבות fooled him. As it is written: 'ה׳ said, Who will trick אחאב so that he goes up and falls at רמות גלעד? And the spirit came out and stood before ה׳ and said, I will trick him. And He said, You will trick him and you will succeed. Go out and do so.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the example. If a spirit from Heaven fooled צדקיה, why is he counted as a false prophet?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים in מלכים say God allowed a spirit to mislead אחאב's prophets. So צדקיה seems to be an innocent victim, not someone who made up a prophecy. Step 25 answers this, after two side comments on the פסוק.
steps.confusionAlert: Steps 23-24 first explain words in the פסוק about the spirit. The answer to why צדקיה is still guilty comes in step 25: he should have noticed that all the prophets used identical wording.

phrases.english: What should he have done?
The spirit of Navot misled him,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ מִי יְפַתֶּה אֶת אַחְאָב
phrases.english: as it is written: "And ה׳ said: Who will trick Achav,
so that he goes up and falls at Ramot Gilad?"
phrases.notes: מלכים א 22:20-22

phrases.english: "And the spirit came out and stood before ה׳,
and said: I will trick him."
"And He said: You will trick him and you will succeed;
go out and do so."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the example given in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: Calling צדקיה a prophet who said what he did not hear.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A spirit from Heaven fooled him, so he seems blameless.

steps.title: What 'go out' means
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that 'צא' means the spirit had to leave God's presence.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: What does 'go out' mean? Go out from My presence.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה explains an extra word in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God could have just said 'do so.' The added word 'go out' teaches that the spirit was sent away from God's presence because it offered to trick.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: What is "go out"?
Go out from My presence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a word in the פסוק quoted in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'צא' means the spirit was sent away from God's presence.

steps.title: Whose spirit it was
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the spirit that tricked אחאב was the spirit of נבות היזרעאלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: What spirit was it? רבי יוחנן said: The spirit of נבות היזרעאלי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which spirit the פסוק is talking about, and רבי יוחנן answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'the spirit,' as if it is a known spirit. רבי יוחנן says it was נבות, whom אחאב had killed. This explains why step 22 called it 'רוח נבות.'

keyTerms.meaning: The man whose vineyard אַחְאָב took after having him killed

phrases.english: What spirit was it?
Rabbi Yochanan said:
The spirit of Navot of Yizre'el.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the פסוק by naming the spirit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The spirit that tricked אחאב was the spirit of נבות.

steps.title: צדקיה should have noticed: real prophets never use identical wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says צדקיה was still responsible. He should have checked the prophecy using רבי יצחק's rule that two prophets never prophesy in the exact same style.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should have looked carefully, using the teaching of רבי יצחק. רבי יצחק said: one message can come to several prophets, but two prophets never say it in the same words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 22: what could צדקיה have done? He could have checked carefully, because there is a sign that shows a prophecy is false.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 showed that a spirit tricked צדקיה, which seemed to excuse him. Here the גמרא says he still had a test he could use. Real prophets may get the same message, but each one says it in his own words.

keyTerms.meaning: A message or a style of saying it (used both ways here)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why a false prophet who was tricked can still be held responsible. There was a clear sign he ignored.

phrases.english: He should have examined carefully,
phrases.notes: 'He' is צדקיה בן כנענה from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: following the teaching of Rabbi Yitzchak,
as Rabbi Yitzchak said:
One message comes to several prophets,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין שְׁנֵי נְבִיאִים מִתְנַבְּאִין בְּסִיגְנוֹן אֶחָד.
phrases.english: but two prophets do not prophesy in the same wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question of Step 22 after the side comments of Steps 23-24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the person had a way to know, so he is still responsible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because a spirit from God tricked צדקיה, he could not have done anything differently.
steps.terutzMaskana: He should have noticed that all the prophets used the exact same words, which is a sign of false prophecy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Many prophets can receive one message, but no two prophets express it in identical wording.

steps.title: Example of one message in two styles, applied to אחאב's prophets
steps.stepSummary: עובדיה and ירמיה give the same message in different words. אחאב's prophets all used the same words, so their prophecy was empty.
steps.simpleTranslation: עובדיה said: 'The pride of your heart has tricked you.' ירמיה said: 'Your terribleness has tricked you, the pride of your heart.' These prophets all said the same thing in the same words, so we learn that what they said was worth nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows רבי יצחק's rule with a real example from two true prophets. Then it uses the rule on the prophets of אחאב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עובדיה and ירמיה share one message, but ירמיה adds 'תפלצתך' and changes the wording. That is how real prophecy works. אחאב's prophets all spoke in exactly the same words, and that proves they were false.

keyTerms.meaning: Your terribleness (the fear you cause others)

phrases.english: Ovadiah said:
"The pride of your heart has tricked you."
phrases.notes: עובדיה 1:3

phrases.english: Yirmiyah said:
"Your terribleness has tricked you,
the pride of your heart."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 49:16

phrases.english: And these, since all of them were saying it the same way,
phrases.notes: 'These' are the prophets of אחאב, together with צדקיה.

phrases.english: learn from it that they were saying nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an example of רבי יצחק's rule and applies it to the case of צדקיה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Identical wording among many prophets shows the prophecy is false.

steps.title: Maybe צדקיה did not know this rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: perhaps צדקיה did not know רבי יצחק's rule, so how can we blame him?
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe he did not know this teaching of רבי יצחק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on Step 25. Blaming צדקיה only makes sense if he knew the sign of a false prophecy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said צדקיה should have checked. But you can only be expected to use a test you know about. If he never heard the rule, he still seems blameless.

phrases.english: Maybe he did not know
this teaching of Rabbi Yitzchak?

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא לָא הֲוָה יָדַע לֵיהּ לְהָא דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim of Step 25 that צדקיה should have known better.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that צדקיה was responsible for not noticing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person cannot be blamed for not using a rule he never knew.

steps.title: יהושפט said the rule out loud right there
steps.stepSummary: יהושפט was present and told them the rule he received from his family. So צדקיה had heard it.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהושפט was there and told them. As it says: 'And יהושפט said: Is there not another prophet of ה׳ here?' אחאב said to him: 'But there are all these!' יהושפט answered: 'This is what I received from my grandfather's house: one message comes to several prophets, but two prophets do not prophesy in the same wording.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. יהושפט said the rule out loud right in front of everyone, so צדקיה cannot claim he did not know it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that יהושפט was not satisfied with 400 prophets and asked for another. When אחאב objected, יהושפט explained why, using the same rule as רבי יצחק. He said it came down from his family, the house of דוד, so צדקיה heard the warning directly.

keyTerms.meaning: King of יהודה, who was with אחאב
Is there not another prophet here?
I have a tradition, I received
From the house of my father's father

steps.whatToRemember: צדקיה was guilty because the sign of false prophecy (identical wording) was obvious, and יהושפט even said it out loud in front of him.

phrases.english: Yehoshafat was there,
and he told them.
As it is written:
"And Yehoshafat said:
Is there not another prophet of ה׳ here?"
phrases.notes: מלכים א 22:7

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא אִיכָּא כֹּל הָנֵי.
phrases.english: He said to him: But there are all these!
phrases.notes: Here אחאב is speaking, pointing to his 400 prophets.

phrases.english: He said to him:
This is what I received from the house of my father's father:
One message comes to several prophets,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין שְׁנֵי נְבִיאִים מִתְנַבְּאִים בְּסִיגְנוֹן אֶחָד.
phrases.english: but two prophets do not prophesy in the same wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual answer based on a פסוק: he was told the rule directly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: צדקיה may not have known the rule, so he would not be to blame.
steps.terutzMaskana: יהושפט stated the rule in front of everyone, so צדקיה knew it and is responsible.

steps.title: Next case of the משנה: חנניה and ירמיה's prophecy about עילם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the משנה's case of one who prophesies what was not said to him, with the example of חנניה בן עזור. It begins with ירמיה's real prophecy about עילם.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who prophesies what was not said to him': for example, חנניה בן עזור. ירמיה was standing in the upper market and saying: 'So says ה׳ [of hosts]: Behold, I am breaking the bow of עילם.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the next case in the משנה. It sets up the story by telling us what ירמיה really prophesied, which prepares for what חנניה does next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier case, צדקיה, was a prophet who said what he did not hear at all. This case is different: חנניה heard a real prophecy, the one about עילם, but it was said to ירמיה, not to him. The setup matters because his false prophecy grows out of ירמיה's true one.

keyTerms.meaning: One who prophesies what was not said to him
A false prophet in the time of ירמיה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with צדקיה. He said something no prophet ever heard. חנניה took a real prophecy given to ירמיה and built on it himself.

phrases.english: One who prophesies what was not said to him:
for example, Chananyah son of Azzur,
for Yirmiyah was standing in the upper market
and saying:
"So says ה׳ [of hosts]:
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording. It matches the wording of the פסוק.

phrases.english: Behold, I am breaking the bow of Eilam."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 49:35

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמִּתְנַבֵּא מַה שֶּׁלֹּא נֶאֱמַר לוֹ: כְּגוֹן חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן עַזּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the צדקיה case and goes to the next case of the משנה, like Step 21 did for the earlier case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנניה בן עזור is the example of one who prophesies what was not said to him.

steps.title: חנניה builds his own קל וחומר and announces it as prophecy
steps.stepSummary: חנניה reasoned that if God would break עילם, בבל's helper, then surely He would break בבל itself. He then announced this in God's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנניה made a קל וחומר on his own: if about עילם, which only came to help בבל, God said 'I am breaking the bow of עילם,' then the Babylonians themselves, all the more so. He went to the lower market and said: 'So says ה׳: I have broken the yoke of the king of בבל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows exactly how חנניה sinned. He took ירמיה's prophecy, figured out a conclusion with his own logic, and then said it as if God had told it to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic itself sounds reasonable, but it was his own reasoning, not a prophecy he received. Saying 'כה אמר ה׳' over his own conclusion is exactly 'prophesying what was not said to him.' The 'upper market' and 'lower market' show him repeating, in a nearby place, a message he took from ירמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: He made a קל וחומר on his own
The yoke of the king of Bavel

steps.whatToRemember: A prophet may not present his own reasoning as God's word. Even a logical קל וחומר, when it is announced as prophecy, makes him a false prophet.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the line between true prophecy and a prophet's own reasoning: only what God actually said to him may be said in God's name.

phrases.english: Chananyah made a kal vachomer on his own:
If Eilam,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא בָּא אֶלָּא לַעֲזוֹר אֶת בָּבֶל
phrases.english: which came only to help Bavel,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
"Behold, I am breaking the bow of Eilam,"
then the Kasdim themselves,
phrases.notes: The כשדים are the Babylonians, the main enemy.

phrases.english: all the more so.
He came to the lower market
and said:
"So says ה׳, etc.:
I have broken the yoke of the king of Bavel."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 28:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in Step 29 and shows how חנניה's false prophecy came about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנניה turned his own קל וחומר into a prophecy in God's name, which is prophesying what was not said to him.

steps.title: רב פפא asks: this was not said to any other prophet either
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי: חנניה's prophecy about בבל was never told to any prophet, so it does not fit the משנה's case of a prophecy that was said to someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But this prophecy was not said to his fellow prophet either!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא questions whether חנניה really fits the משנה's category of 'what was not said to him.' That category means a prophecy that God gave to someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates two cases: a prophet who makes up something no one heard, and a prophet who repeats something that was told to another prophet. חנניה only reasoned his message out from ירמיה's prophecy about עילם. Nobody, including ירמיה, was ever told that בבל would be broken. So רב פפא asks why חנניה is not placed in the first case instead.

keyTerms.meaning: to his fellow, meaning another prophet

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
This was not said to his fellow either!
phrases.notes: 'His fellow' means another prophet, like ירמיה. In the משנה's case, the prophecy is supposed to have been said to someone else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim that חנניה's reasoning from step 30 fits the משנה's category of 'what was not said to him.'
steps.kashyaTarget: Using חנניה as the example for 'one who prophesies what was not said to him.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That category requires a prophecy that was told to another prophet. חנניה's conclusion about Bavel was never told to anyone, so the example does not seem to fit.

steps.title: A message that can be learned by קל וחומר counts as already said
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that a conclusion you can draw by קל וחומר from ירמיה's prophecy counts as if God had said it to ירמיה. So חנניה took a message that belonged to someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Since a קל וחומר was given to be learned out, it is as if it had been said to ירמיה. חנניה is the one to whom it was not said.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends the example. A message you can learn by קל וחומר is treated as part of what God actually told ירמיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר is a proper way to learn out a point, so its conclusion counts as included in the original prophecy. That means the message about בבל was in effect told to ירמיה. חנניה's sin was announcing it as though God had told him directly, and that is exactly the משנה's case.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'how much more so' argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
to be learned out or expounded

phrases.english: He said to him:
Since a kal vachomer was given to be learned out,
it is like something that was said to him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' here is ירמיה, who received the prophecy about עילם.

phrases.english: He is the one to whom it was not said.
phrases.notes: 'He' is חנניה. The message belonged to ירמיה, not to him.

steps.whatToRemember: A conclusion that can be drawn by קל וחומר from a prophecy counts as part of that prophecy. חנניה is guilty because he claimed God told it to him.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines what counts as 'said to another': a conclusion that can be learned by קל וחומר counts as said.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only words God actually spoke count as 'said to another prophet,' so חנניה's reasoned conclusion would not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: A קל וחומר conclusion is treated as said to ירמיה. חנניה fits the case of 'what was not said to him.'

steps.title: Example for prophesying in the name of idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the example for the משנה's case of one who prophesies in the name of עבודה זרה: the prophets of the בעל.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who prophesies in the name of עבודה זרה: for example, the prophets of the בעל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next case in the משנה and gives a well-known example from תנ"ך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is in the משנה's list of prophets put to death by a court. The example is the prophets of the בעל, who claimed to speak in the name of an idol. No discussion follows; the גמרא just names the example.

keyTerms.meaning: the prophets of the בעל, an idol

phrases.english: One who prophesies in the name of idol worship:
for example, the prophets of the Baal.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמִּתְנַבֵּא בְּשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כְּגוֹן נְבִיאֵי הַבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the חנניה case to the next case listed in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prophets of the בעל are the example of one who prophesies in the name of עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Example for holding back a prophecy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the example for the משנה's case of one who holds back his prophecy: יונה בן אמיתי.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who holds back his prophecy: for example, יונה בן אמיתי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the משנה's list of those who receive death from Heaven and gives the first example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding back a prophecy means a prophet does not deliver the message God gave him. יונה ran away instead of bringing God's message to נינוה, so he is the classic example.

keyTerms.meaning: one who holds back or suppresses
the prophet יונה, son of אמיתי

phrases.english: One who holds back his prophecy:
for example, Jonah son of Amittai.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת נְבוּאָתוֹ כְּגוֹן יוֹנָה בֶּן אֲמִיתַּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues giving examples for the cases in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יונה בן אמיתי is the example of a prophet who holds back his prophecy.

steps.title: Starting the example for ignoring a prophet's words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins the example for the משנה's case of one who ignores a prophet's words. The example itself continues in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who ignores the words of a prophet: for example...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא names the next case from the משנה and starts to give an example, which comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is about a listener who does not obey a true prophet's instructions, not about a prophet. It is also in the משנה's list of those who receive death from Heaven. The text here stops at 'for example,' so the actual case is still coming.

keyTerms.meaning: one who ignores or lets go of

phrases.english: And one who ignores the words of a prophet:
for example...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of examples for the cases in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גמרא is about to give the example of one who ignores a prophet's words.
